clues: This place lies on flat land near a river in the middle of the country. An old famed road, Route 66, runs right through it.
Hot, wet summers and cold, snowy winters both hit this place. It sits at the far edge of Tornado Alley, so strong storms roll through in the warm months.
The seat of government moved here in 1839, drawn by its spot at the center of the state. Local lawmakers worked hard to win the move here.
Abraham Lincoln lived in this town for 24 years. In 1861 he left it to be President.
The lawmakers of Illinois meet in this place to make state laws. The governor of Illinois keeps an office here too.
